title: Large coverage fluctuations in Google Scholar: a case study
extended_summary:
This paper examines a major fluctuation in Google Scholar’s coverage, focusing on a sharp drop in indexed documents and citation counts in the field of Astronomy and Astrophysics during 2019 and the subsequent recovery by 2020. The authors are concerned with the instability of Google Scholar as a discovery and bibliometric tool, especially because the platform can remove documents from its index when its crawlers cannot access them and because its coverage is not transparently documented.

The study uses a longitudinal observational approach based on three datasets of citing documents to 10 highly cited Astronomy & Astrophysics papers from Google Scholar Classic Papers, with data extracted in 2018, 2019, and 2020. The authors matched citing records across years using Google Scholar IDs, URLs, DOIs, and title-author similarity, then analyzed which citations disappeared and later reappeared. They also grouped missing citations by publisher to investigate whether the coverage loss was concentrated in particular sources.

There were no human participants; the unit of analysis was bibliographic records and citation links in Google Scholar. The context is the scholarly indexing ecosystem, especially large publishers in Astronomy and Astrophysics such as EDP Sciences, the American Astronomical Society, and others whose documents remained on the web but temporarily disappeared from Google Scholar. The paper is explicitly marked as not peer-reviewed.

The main conclusion is that Google Scholar experienced a substantial but temporary indexing failure in 2019 that removed many documents from major publishers despite those documents remaining available online, strongly suggesting an error on Google Scholar’s side. Most missing citations reappeared by 2020, but the delay of many months highlights a significant limitation of Google Scholar for reproducible literature searching and bibliometric analysis.
quality_tier_rationale: The provided document is not the requested secondary-school writing study. It is a non-peer-reviewed bibliometric case study about Google Scholar coverage fluctuations, with no educational intervention and no student learning design relevant to the K-12 evidence framework.
impact_tier_rationale: This paper reports no educational intervention effects on student outcomes; therefore it provides no usable impact evidence for secondary-school writing.
